title: Detecting Spillovers in Linear-in-Means Models on Graphs of Growing Degree

proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and independently audited a computable quadratic test with variance order d^2/n, a matching all-test Hellinger converse, the local separation rate sqrt(d) n^(-1/4), and the exact d=o(sqrt(n)) consistency boundary on connected regular graphs of girth at least five. It also generalized the converse to arbitrary minimum-degree-two graphs through a capped water-filling functional, with no false headline or crux laundering found. The result stopped because this sound package was rated subfield rather than field; a future re-raise must add a matching irregular-network upper frontier and should reframe Gao et al.'s d_max^5/n result as an asserted comparator.
tldr: From one Bernoulli\((1/2)\) experiment, the matched local separation rate on observed connected \(d\)-regular graphs of girth at least five is \(\sqrt d\,n^{-1/4}\): the quadratic score has finite-sample level and power guarantees, and a legal fixed-schedule mixture gives an all-test lower bound. On the anchor arbitrary-network class with every \(d_i\ge2\), the lower bound is graph by graph: \(R_G(\rho)\ge\max\{0,1-600\sqrt{J_G(\rho)}\}\) for \(0<\rho\le1\), where \(J_G\) is an explicit capped convex program. Its uncapped value is \(n^2\rho^4/\sum_i d_i^2\) only when the water-filling allocation remains feasible. The regular high-girth class has \(d\le\sqrt{n-1}\), so this recovers the matched scale there and yields consistency against every fixed legal separation exactly when \(d=o(\sqrt n)\). No sharp fixed-error constant or arbitrary-network upper rate is claimed.
gap: The closest paper already defines the bounded heterogeneous linear-in-means alternative, the squared spillover target, and the quadratic estimator, but proves only an \(O(d_{\max}^5/n)\) MSE bound and \(d_{\max}=o(n^{1/5})\) sufficiency. No inspected work gives a matching all-test local separation lower bound under arbitrary bounded fixed-schedule nuisance coefficients.
fill: Prove the exact closed-neighborhood covariance cases, derive uniform \(d^2/n\) variance control and a computable finite-sample test, establish a legal compact-support Hellinger mixture bound of order \(n\rho^4/d^2\), and combine them into the local minimax rate and exact growing-degree consistency boundary on explicit feasible graph sequences.
